To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have isolated and sequenced a phytochrome-encodig gene from Zea mays and have compared its structure and function with other phytochromes.
the structure of the maize phytochromes is highly conserved with other monocots and that the maize phyA promoter contains several conserved sequence elements that may play a role in phy expression.
the maize phy gene has been cloned and characterized.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure, regulation and function of phytochrome genes in maize and their evolutionary relationship to other monocot and dicot phytochrome- encoding genes.
understanding the molecular basis for light-regulated expression of the phy gene family and its role in the regulation of plant development.
the isolation and characterization of the maize phy gene family, and with the elucidation of the regulatory mechanisms that control their expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the phyA gene is a typical phy gene.
maize phyA1 has a structure highly conserved with respect to other monocot phy genes and that the phy gene is down-regulated by light.
the maize phyA gene is highly homologous to the phyA genes of other species, but the phyA1 promoter is different from that of other monocot phy genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
phyA1 is a typical monocot phy, with an overall sequence identity of 88% to the type A phy of Avena.
maize phyA1, like the other monocot phy genes, is expressed in etiolated tissues and is down-regulated by light.
phyA1 and phyA2 are the two functional phy genes in maize, phyA1 is a type A gene and phyA2 is a type B gene.
The main takeaway from our work is that
phyA1 is a functional phyA gene in maize and that phyA1 mRNA is regulated by light in a manner similar to the phyA gene of Avena.
phytochrome gene regulation is not as conserved as phytochrome gene sequence.
the phy gene family is highly conserved between monocot and dicot plant species.
